  mutate(
    label    = factor(label, levels = scen_meta$label),
    hab_type = factor(hab_type,
                      levels = c("Cold only", "Cold + Warm", "Cold + Warm (high P)"))
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(cols      = starts_with("mean_p_"),
               names_to  = "component",
               values_to = "mean_p",
               names_prefix = "mean_p_") |>
  mutate(component = factor(component,
    levels = c("sg",   "temp",                "starv",               "age"),
    labels = c("Size (p_sg)", "Temperature (p_temp)",
               "Condition (p_starv)", "Age (p_age)")))

Version 1: survival source in rows, cold proportion in columns, scenario as colour. Note the longer period of low summer size-based survival in the cold+warm relative to cold-only scenarios, particularly as the cold patch shrinks

Code 
dsh_brks <- c(0, 61, 122, 183, 244, 305, 365)
dsh_labs <- c("May","Jul","Sep","Nov","Jan","Mar","May")

# Seasonal bands on a daily (dsh) x-axis.
# Season boundaries from make_season_layers() are in msb units (months since
# April birth); multiply by 365/12 to convert to days since hatch.
# ymin/ymax span all survival probability rows; facet clipping handles the rest.
make_season_layers_dsh <- function(n_years = 1L, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf) {
  # Season boundaries converted from msb to dsh (days since hatch).
  # 1 msb = 365/12 ≈ 30.44 days. Default ymin/ymax = -Inf/Inf: fills each
  # panel's full height regardless of free y-scale (works on linear axes only;
  # log axes require finite bounds — use make_season_layers() instead).
  dpm       <- 365 / 12
  xmin_tmpl <- (c( 0.5,  1.5,  4.5,  7.5, 10.5)-1) * dpm
  xmax_tmpl <- (c( 1.5,  4.5,  7.5, 10.5, 13.5)-1) * dpm
  fill_tmpl <- c("#A8D5A2", "#F5C543", "#C8A96E", "#AEC6E8", "#A8D5A2")
  unlist(lapply(0:(n_years - 1L), \(y)
    lapply(seq_along(fill_tmpl), \(i)
      annotate("rect",
               xmin  = xmin_tmpl[i] + y * 365,
               xmax  = xmax_tmpl[i] + y * 365,
               ymin  = ymin, ymax = ymax,
               fill  = fill_tmpl[i],
               alpha = 0.22)
    )
  ), recursive = FALSE)
}

ggplot(filter(surv_daily_df, component != "Age (p_age)"),

  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_number(accuracy = 0.001)) +
  labs(
    x       = NULL,
    y       = "Mean daily survival probability",
    title   = "Daily survival probability by source \u2014 age-0 fish, first year of life",
    caption = "n \u2248 45 cohort-years per scenario."

By calculating cumulative log-survival (product of daily mean \(p\)) over the entire “summer” (birth to Oct 31) by source, we can see that size-based survival (due to density dependent effects on growth) dominates, with increasing survival costs as the cold patch shrinks, but only for cold+warm scenarios with elevated fry production

Code 
# Computed from surv_daily_df (surv-daily-data chunk)
cum_surv_df <- surv_daily_df |>
  filter(component %in% c("Size (p_sg)", "Condition (p_starv)")) |>
  group_by(label, prop_cold, hab_type, component) |>
  summarise(
    summer = prod(mean_p[dsh <  183L]),
    winter = prod(mean_p[dsh >= 183L]),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(c(summer, winter),
               names_to  = "season",
               values_to = "cum_surv") |>
  mutate(
    log_loss = log(cum_surv),
    season   = factor(season,
                      levels = c("summer", "winter"),
                      labels = c("Summer (birth \u2192 Nov)",
                                 "Winter (Nov \u2192 May)"))
  )

  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.4, color = "grey40", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.85) +

  facet_wrap(~component, nrow = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = hab_cols, name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0.05, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 0.95),
                     labels = scales::label_percent(accuracy = 1),
                     transform = "reverse") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_number(accuracy = 0.1)) +
  labs(
    x       = "Cold habitat proportion",
    y       = "Cumulative log-survival",
    title   = "Cumulative summer (birth \u2192 Oct 31) survival by source \u2014 age-0 fish",
    caption = "Cumulative survival = \u03a0(daily mean p) over the window, then log-transformed.\n0 = no mortality; more negative = more loss."
  ) +

Fall “recruitment”

Collectively, this creates a substantial early life bottleneck, such that the number of surviving to the end of the first summer is purely a function of cold habitat availability, despite substantial differences in initial fry production owing to the relative availability of warm habitat.

Code

  mean_n_age0, pmax(mean_n_age0 - sd_n_age0, 0), mean_n_age0 + sd_n_age0,

14.4.0.2 Warm habitat availability mitigates winter losses

After November 1, all scenario classes enter their first winter with effectively the same number of age-0 fish — a direct consequence of cold habitat constraining summer recruitment. From this common baseline, the cold-only and cold+warm scenarios diverge sharply by the end of winter/early spring. The mechanism is condition-based (starvation) mortality: fish restricted to cold habitat cannot sustain adequate energy intake through winter, losing body mass until condition drops below the threshold that drives survival penalties. Fish with access to warm habitat can and do use it for continued foraging, (mostly) maintaining mass and avoiding further declines in abundance almost entirely.

Habitat use

Fish move from cold to warm in the late fall (Oct-Nov). As cold proportion declines and warm increases, fish are more likely to remain in warm through the winter.

Code

In summary, fish are preferrentially using the warm patch during winter, regardless of cold proportion. Winter densities are greater in the warm patch than in the cold patch, but this difference shrinks as the proportion of cold habitat declines (largely mediated by area).

Density dependence

Fish are basically ~input matching: when warm habitat is rare, higher densities mean increased strength of density dependence (lower DD scalar) in warm. Cold patch DD is stronger for cold-only scenarios relative to cold-warm, because all fish are forced to use cold habitat during winter, while fish in cold+warm scenarios can disperse to warm habitat.

Consumption

During winter, consumption is entirely constrained by cold patch temperature in the cold-only scenarios. In contrast, temperature and density dependence in the warm patch combine to constrain consumption in the cold+warm scenarios. When proportion cold is high (warm habitat is rare), density dependence in the warm habitat is primarily limiting consumption. But when proportion cold is low (warm habitat is abundant), density dependence in the warm habitat is less significant, and temperature becomes the primary constraint. As a result, cold+warm fish feed at higher rates than cold-only fish, and cold+warm consumption increases as cold habitat is increasingly replaced by warm habitat.

Code 
# Decomposition of realized p-value into temperature and density-dependence
# components across the full age-0 year, for both cold and warm patches.
#   Dashed line  = mean_pcmax_adj  (temperature ceiling; DD removed)
#   Solid line   = mean_realized_p (after DD suppression)
#   Shaded gap   = density-dependence suppression alone
# Cold patch: DD gap widens in early summer for cold+warm scenarios (more fish
#   from warm-enabled reproduction flooding into cold habitat).
# Warm patch: temperature ceiling collapses near peak summer (~Jul–Aug) as
#   fncTempDepend approaches 0 near 24°C, independently of density. Cold-only
#   scenarios have no warm patch and are absent from the bottom row.

# Warm patch: color-coded dotted lines at 0.5 (Cold + Warm) and 0.6 (high P).

Growth

Cold-only fish thus experience consistently negative growth rates overwinter, leading to reduce condition across all cold proportions. In contrast, mean winter growth rates for cold-warm fish increase as warm habitat becomes more available (declining density dependent constraints on consumption), and fish are better able to avoid declines in condition.

Spring “recruitment”

After the shared summer bottleneck sets a common Nov. 1 baseline, the cold-only and cold+warm scenarios diverge through winter. Cold-only fish face a second condition-driven mortality episode in late winter/early spring that warm-habitat fish largely avoid. By April 1 — the end of the first year of life — the scenarios separate clearly: cold+warm (and especially high-P) cohorts retain substantially more survivors than cold-only cohorts at equivalent cold proportions, and the divergence grows as warm habitat increases.

Code 
mk_panel(full_df,
  mean_n_apr1, pmax(mean_n_apr1 - sd_n_apr1, 0), mean_n_apr1 + sd_n_apr1,
  "Mean age-0 survivors (May 1)", NULL, show_x = TRUE)

14.4.1 Biomass/wight-at-age

The preceding weight-at-age panels show that cold+warm fish are substantially heavier at a given age than cold-only fish, and the gap widens as warm habitat proportion grows. This section traces the weight-at-age difference mechanistically to supplemental growth opportunities provided by the warm patch — primarily in fall (Sep–Nov) and spring (Mar–May), when warm-patch temperatures allow substantially higher consumption and growth rates than the cold patch.

Figure summary:

  • (A) Mean individual body mass at Oct 1 — the end-point observation.
  • (B) Per-fish specific growth rate by season and patch — warm-patch fish grow faster than cold-patch fish in fall and spring; the advantage scales with warm habitat availability and collapses when the warm patch is too small to relieve density dependence.
  • (C) Seasonal consumption rates by patch — identifies the proximate mechanism: in fall and spring the warm patch sustains a substantially higher temperature ceiling and realized p-value than the cold patch; density-dependent suppression erodes the realized advantage as the warm patch shrinks.
  • (D) Synthesis scatterplot — warm-patch fall and spring growth rates vs. Oct 1 body mass, directly quantifying the link between seasonal warm-patch growth opportunities and realized weight-at-age.

14.4.1.1 Data

Code 
# Per-fish mean specific growth rate (ggd × 10⁻³ g/g/d) by season × patch.
# Averaged across all surviving fish and experimental-period years.
# Requires ibm_list_mech (defined in the Mechanistic drivers setup chunk).

compute_seasonal_ggd <- function(s) {
  s$df |>
    filter(date >= exp_start_date, survived == 1, !is.na(ggd), floor(age) >= 1) |>
    mutate(
      mo     = month(date),
      season = factor(
        case_when(
          mo %in% c(12,1,2)    ~ "Winter",
          mo %in% c(3:5)       ~ "Spring",
          mo %in% c(6:8)       ~ "Summer",
          mo %in% c(9:11)      ~ "Fall"
        ),
        levels = c("Spring", "Summer", "Fall", "Winter")
      )
    ) |>
    group_by(season, patch) |>
    summarise(mean_ggd = mean(ggd, na.rm = TRUE) * 1000, .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(prop_cold = s$pc, hab_type = s$ht)
}

seasonal_ggd_df <- bind_rows(lapply(ibm_list_live, compute_seasonal_ggd)) |>
  left_join(scen_meta, by = "prop_cold") |>
  mutate(
    label     = factor(label,    levels = scen_meta$label),
    hab_type  = factor(hab_type, levels = c("Cold only", "Cold + Warm", "Cold + Warm (high P)")),
    patch_lab = factor(
      if_else(patch == "warm", "Warm patch", "Cold patch"),
      levels = c("Cold patch", "Warm patch")
    )
  )
Code 
# Seasonal mean consumption-rate summaries by patch for ALL fish (not just age-0).
# Uses the same bioenergetics decomposition as pcmax_age0_df but applied to the
# full population on each simulated date:
#   temperature ceiling:  pcmax_adj  = min(fncTempDepend(temp), pcmax_baseline)
#   density-dep. scalar:  dd_scalar  = K / (K + n_fish_in_patch / patch_area)
#   realized p-value:     realized_p = pcmax_adj * dd_scalar
#
# pcmax baselines: cold patch = 0.5 (all scenarios);
#                  warm patch = 0.5 (Cold+Warm) or 0.6 (high P); NA (Cold only).
# Season definitions match winter-bm-data: Dec–Feb = Winter, Mar–May = Spring,
# Jun–Aug = Summer, Sep–Nov = Fall.

compute_seasonal_p_all <- function(s) {
  a_cold     <- s$pc * 2.0
  a_warm     <- (1 - s$pc) * 2.0
  K          <- base_params$K_cold
  pcmax_cold <- 0.5
  pcmax_warm <- switch(s$ht,
    "Cold + Warm"          = 0.5,
    "Cold + Warm (high P)" = 0.6,
    NA_real_
  )

  s$df |>
    filter(date >= exp_start_date, survived == 1, floor(age) >= 1) |>
    mutate(
      mo     = month(date),
      season = factor(
        case_when(
          mo %in% c(12L, 1L, 2L) ~ "Winter",
          mo %in% c(3:5)          ~ "Spring",
          mo %in% c(6:8)          ~ "Summer",
          mo %in% c(9:11)         ~ "Fall"
        ),
        levels = c("Spring", "Summer", "Fall", "Winter")
      )
    ) |>
    # Reduce to one row per date × patch before computing pcmax quantities
    group_by(date, season, patch) |>
    summarise(n = n(), temp_day = first(temp), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(
      area       = if_else(patch == "cold", a_cold, a_warm),
      pcmax_b    = if_else(patch == "cold", pcmax_cold, pcmax_warm),
      pcmax_adj  = pmin(fncTempDepend(temp_day), pcmax_b),
      dd_scalar  = K / (K + n / area),
      realized_p = pcmax_adj * dd_scalar
    ) |>
    group_by(season, patch) |>
    summarise(
      mean_realized_p = mean(realized_p, na.rm = TRUE),
      mean_pcmax_adj  = mean(pcmax_adj,  na.rm = TRUE),
      mean_dd         = mean(dd_scalar,  na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    mutate(prop_cold = s$pc, hab_type = s$ht)
}

seasonal_p_df <- bind_rows(lapply(ibm_list_live, compute_seasonal_p_all)) |>
  left_join(scen_meta, by = "prop_cold") |>
  mutate(
    label     = factor(label,    levels = scen_meta$label),
    hab_type  = factor(hab_type, levels = c("Cold only", "Cold + Warm", "Cold + Warm (high P)")),
    patch_lab = factor(
      if_else(patch == "warm", "Warm patch", "Cold patch"),
      levels = c("Cold patch", "Warm patch")
    )
  )

# Joined data for the synthesis scatterplot: warm-patch seasonal SGR × weight-per-fish.
# Cold-only scenarios (no warm patch) are excluded from points but provide the
# weight reference band via pop_sum.
wt_ggd_df <- seasonal_ggd_df |>
  filter(
    (hab_type == "Cold only" & patch_lab == "Cold patch") |
    (hab_type != "Cold only" & patch_lab == "Warm patch")
  ) |>
  select(hab_type, prop_cold, label, season, mean_ggd) |>
  left_join(
    pop_sum |>
      mutate(mean_wt_g = mean_b * 1000 / mean_n) |>
      select(hab_type, prop_cold, label, mean_wt_g),
    by = c("hab_type", "prop_cold", "label")
  )

# Cold-only fish are roughly the same size regardless of cold proportion;
# cold+warm fish grow progressively heavier as warm habitat expands.
pop_sum |>
  mutate(mean_wt_g = mean_b * 1000 / mean_n) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = prop_cold, y = mean_wt_g, color = hab_type)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.85) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +

# (B) Per-fish mean specific growth rate by season × patch.
# Row 1 (Warm patch): warm-patch SGR rises steeply with warm-habitat availability
#   in fall and spring, driven by higher temperature ceilings and lower density.
#   The advantage collapses when the warm patch is too small (high prop_cold).
# Row 2 (Cold patch): cold-patch SGR shows the contrasting pattern — strongly
#   suppressed in spring across cold+warm scenarios due to overcrowding when fish
#   return from the warm patch, and consistently negative in winter.
seasonal_ggd_df |>
  ggplot(aes(
    x        = prop_cold,
    y        = mean_ggd,
    color    = hab_type,
    # linetype = patch_lab,
    group    = interaction(hab_type, patch_lab)

  geom_line(linewidth = 0.85) +
  geom_point(size = 2.0) +

  scale_color_manual(values = hab_cols, name = "Scenario") +

Code 
# (C) Seasonal consumption rates by patch: temperature ceiling (dashed) vs
# realized p-value (solid).
# Cold patch: in spring and fall, the temperature ceiling is the primary
#   constraint; the cold-patch ceiling is substantially lower than the warm
#   patch, particularly in fall. Winter cold-patch consumption is strongly
#   temperature-limited (~0.10).
# Warm patch: the temperature ceiling is ~0.5–0.6 year-round; the gap between
#   the dashed ceiling and solid realized p represents density-dependent
#   suppression, which grows as the warm patch shrinks (higher prop_cold).
seasonal_p_df |>
  filter(!is.na(mean_realized_p)) |>

  geom_point(aes(y = mean_realized_p), size = 2.0) +
  facet_grid(patch_lab ~ season) +
  scale_color_manual(values = hab_cols, name = "Scenario") +
  cold_x("Proportion cold habitat") +
  labs(

    title   = "(C) Seasonal consumption rates by patch",
    caption = "Solid = realized p  |  Dashed = temperature ceiling (pcmax_adj)"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey92"),
    legend.position  = "right"
  )
Code 
# (D) Synthesis scatterplot: warm-patch fall and spring SGR (x) vs mean
# individual weight at Oct 1 (y), faceted by season.
# Fall panel: clear positive monotonic relationship — as fall warm-patch growth
#   rate increases with warm-habitat availability, Oct 1 body mass rises
#   proportionally.  The 5% warm scenarios fall below the cold-only band,
#   showing that a tiny overcrowded warm patch confers no weight benefit.
# Spring panel: positive but non-monotonic — the spring warm-patch advantage
#   is largest for intermediate warm habitat fractions; at 95% cold the spring
#   warm-patch SGR reverses because the tiny warm patch is severely density-
#   suppressed and cold-patch fish benefit from the excess warm-habitat area.
# Cold-only scenarios (shaded band) cluster near 224–232 g regardless of cold
# proportion — the body-size baseline when no warm-patch growth is possible.

cold_only_wt_range <- wt_ggd_df |>
  filter(hab_type == "Cold only") |>
  summarise(ymin = min(mean_wt_g), ymax = max(mean_wt_g))

wt_ggd_df |>
  filter(hab_type != "Cold only"#, season %in% c("Fall", "Spring")
         ) |>
  mutate(warm_lab = paste0(round((1 - prop_cold) * 100), "% warm")) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = mean_ggd, y = mean_wt_g, color = hab_type)) +
  annotate("rect",
           xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf,
           ymin = cold_only_wt_range$ymin,
           ymax = cold_only_wt_range$ymax,
           fill = hab_cols["Cold only"], alpha = 0.18) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dotted", color = "grey50") +
  geom_line(aes(group = hab_type), linewidth = 0.75, linetype = "dashed", alpha = 0.55) +
  geom_point(size = 3.2) +
  geom_text_repel(
    aes(label = warm_lab),
    size               = 2.8,
    box.padding        = 0.30,
    point.padding      = 0.15,
    min.segment.length = 0.2,
    force              = 2,
    max.overlaps       = 15
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~season, scales = "free_x", nrow = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = hab_cols,
    name   = NULL,
    limits = c("Cold + Warm", "Cold + Warm (high P)")
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(165, 720)) +
  labs(
    x        = expression("Warm-patch mean SGR" ~ (g ~ g^{-1} ~ d^{-1} %*% 10^{-3})),
    y        = "Mean individual weight at Oct 1 (g)",
    title    = "(D) Seasonal warm-patch growth rate vs. fall body mass",
    subtitle = "Shaded band = cold-only weight range (\u223c224\u2013232 g); labels show warm habitat proportion"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey92"),
    legend.position  = "bottom"
  )

14.4.2 Density-mediated thinning paradox

At 95% cold habitat, Cold + Warm scenarios produce roughly half the spawner abundance and biomass of Cold Only — a counterintuitive result given that warm habitat should, in principle, increase growth and reproductive output. The four panels below trace the causal mechanism step by step. Warm habitat reliably increases first-winter survival (A), but the extra survivors crowd cold habitat during summer (B). At high cold proportions, this density cost outweighs the limited growth benefit from a tiny warm patch, leaving Cold + Warm fish smaller than Cold Only fish at Oct 1 (C). As the warm patch grows larger (lower cold proportions), it provides enough spring and summer growth to more than offset the crowding cost — Cold + Warm fish become progressively larger than Cold Only fish (C) — and spawning participation follows suit (D). The tipping point falls between 95% and 75% cold, i.e., when warm habitat constitutes at least ~20–25% of total area.

Code 
# ── Per-scenario summaries ────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# (A) First-winter survival: delta-method SD from full_df
surv_summ <- full_df |>
  mutate(
    hab_type  = factor(hab_type, levels = c("Cold only", "Cold + Warm", "Cold + Warm (high P)")),
    mean_surv = mean_n_apr1 / mean_n_age0,
    sd_surv   = mean_surv * sqrt((sd_n_apr1 / mean_n_apr1)^2 +
                                   (sd_n_age0 / mean_n_age0)^2)
  ) |>
  select(hab_type, prop_cold, mean_surv, sd_surv)

# (B) Age-1+ summer cold-habitat fish-days with per-year SD
age1_summ <- purrr::map_dfr(ibm_list_live, function(scen) {
  scen$df |>
    filter(date >= exp_start_date,
           month(date) %in% 7:9, patch == "cold",
           age >= 1, survived == 1) |>
    group_by(yr = year(date)) |>
    summarise(fish_days = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
    summarise(mean_fd = mean(fish_days), sd_fd = sd(fish_days)) |>
    mutate(hab_type = scen$ht, prop_cold = scen$pc)
}) |>
  mutate(hab_type = factor(hab_type,
                           levels = c("Cold only", "Cold + Warm", "Cold + Warm (high P)")))

# (C) Mean individual weight of age-1+ fish at Oct 1 — net outcome of crowding vs warm growth
wt_summ <- exp_oct1 |>
  filter(age_class >= 1) |>
  group_by(hab_type, prop_cold, year) |>
  summarise(mean_wt = mean(weight), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(hab_type, prop_cold) |>
  summarise(mean_wt_g = mean(mean_wt), sd_wt_g = sd(mean_wt), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(hab_type = factor(hab_type,
                           levels = c("Cold only", "Cold + Warm", "Cold + Warm (high P)")))

# (D) Spawning participation: per-year spawners from spawn log / mean Apr 15 count
apr15_n <- purrr::map_dfr(ibm_list_live, function(scen) {
  scen$df |>
    filter(date >= exp_start_date,
           month(date) == 4, day(date) == 15, survived == 1) |>
    count(yr = year(date), name = "n_apr15") |>
    summarise(mean_n_apr15 = mean(n_apr15)) |>
    mutate(hab_type = scen$ht, prop_cold = scen$pc)
}) |>
  mutate(hab_type = factor(hab_type,
                           levels = c("Cold only", "Cold + Warm", "Cold + Warm (high P)")))

spawn_part_summ <- exp_spawn_yr |>
  left_join(apr15_n |> select(hab_type, prop_cold, mean_n_apr15),
            by = c("hab_type", "prop_cold")) |>
  mutate(prop_spawn = n_spawners / mean_n_apr15) |>
  group_by(hab_type, prop_cold) |>
  summarise(mean_prop = mean(prop_spawn), sd_prop = sd(prop_spawn), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(hab_type = factor(hab_type,
                           levels = c("Cold only", "Cold + Warm", "Cold + Warm (high P)")))

}

rl <- function(data, x, y, lo, hi) {
  list(
    geom_ribbon(data = data,
                aes(x = {{ x }}, ymin = {{ lo }}, ymax = {{ hi }},
                    fill = hab_type, group = hab_type),
                alpha = 0.18, color = NA),
    geom_line(data  = data,
              aes(x = {{ x }}, y = {{ y }},
                  color = hab_type, group = hab_type),
              linewidth = 0.9),
    geom_point(data = data,
               aes(x = {{ x }}, y = {{ y }}, color = hab_type),
               size = 2.8, shape = 16)
  )
}

This figure needs refinement: they show the cost of extra survivors (more crowding, lower cold-habitat growth) without showing how that cost is distributed between cold and warm habitats. As cold proportion falls, more warm habitat is available and fish that use it grow faster.

```{r, include = FALSE, cache = FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
```

**Purpose:** Compare emergent population outcomes across simulation runs.

**Questions:** 

- How does access to seasonally warm habitat influence population abundance, biomass, and weight-at-age?
- How does this change as the availability of perennially cold habitat shrinks and warm habitat expands? 
- What are the mechanisms driving differences in population outcomes across cold/warm habitat configurations?


## Setup

Load each result .rds object and bind directly into a list. Using a helper function ensures each `res` object is freed from memory as soon as `ibm_long` is extracted, avoiding duplicate references that would force R to copy the data frames.
```{r}
#| cache: false

# Helper: read one scenario, extract ibm_long and spawn_log, and free res before returning
load_scen <- function(path, pc, ht, pcmax_cold, pcmax_warm) {
  res <- readRDS(path)
  list(df = res$ibm_long, spawn_log = res$spawn_log,
       pc = pc, ht = ht, pcmax_cold = pcmax_cold, pcmax_warm = pcmax_warm)
}
```

Summarize within each scenario before combining to avoid loading all fifteen full data frames into memory simultaneously. The Oct 1 census data (1 row per fish per year) and the patch-level growth totals (1 row per year × patch) are the only data structures that need to be combined across scenarios.
```{r}
#| cache: false

# ── Scenario metadata ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
scen_meta <- tibble(
  scen_key  = c("100", "95", "75", "50", "25", "10", "05"),
  label     = c("100% cold", "95% cold", "75% cold", "50% cold", "25% cold", "10% cold", "5% cold"),
  prop_cold = c(1.00, 0.95, 0.75, 0.50, 0.25, 0.10, 0.05)
)

# factor levels
pc_levels <- c(1.00, 0.95, 0.75, 0.50, 0.25, 0.10, 0.05)
pc_levels_mech <- c(1.00, 0.95, 0.75, 0.50, 0.25, 0.10, 0.05)
pc_labels_mech <- c("100% cold", "95% cold", "75% cold", "50% cold", "25% cold", "10% cold", "5% cold")

scen_pal <- setNames(
  hcl.colors(7, "Zissou 1"),
  scen_meta$label
)

# Linetype and shape palettes for habitat availability
hab_cols  <- c("Cold only" = "#6BAED6",  "Cold + Warm" = "#FC8D59",   "Cold + Warm (high P)" = "#B30000")
hab_lty   <- c("Cold only" = "solid" ,   "Cold + Warm" = "solid",     "Cold + Warm (high P)" = "solid")
hab_shape <- c("Cold only" = 16,         "Cold + Warm" = 16,          "Cold + Warm (high P)" = 16)

# Helper: derive scen_key string from numeric prop_cold
pc_to_key <- function(pc) sprintf("%02d", round(pc * 100))

# Helper: TRUE if the population went extinct before the experimental period
# (ibm_long is NULL, has no rows, or lacks a date column)
ibm_is_empty <- function(ibm_long) {
  is.null(ibm_long) || nrow(ibm_long) == 0 || !"date" %in% names(ibm_long)
}

# Per-scenario extinction flag
scen_extinct <- purrr::map_dfr(ibm_list_mech, function(scen) {
  tibble(scen_key = pc_to_key(scen$pc),
         hab_type = scen$ht,
         extinct  = ibm_is_empty(scen$df))
})

# Scenarios with data (extinct scenarios dropped) for chunks that need ibm_long rows
ibm_list_live <- Filter(\(s) !ibm_is_empty(s$df), ibm_list_mech)

# Helper: extract Oct 1 experimental-period rows from one ibm_long
# Filtering before bind_rows() keeps only ~1/365th of each data frame.
extract_oct1_exp <- function(ibm_long, scen_key) {
  if (ibm_is_empty(ibm_long)) return(tibble())
  ibm_long |>
    filter(date >= exp_start_date,
           month(date) == 10, day(date) == 1,
           survived == 1) |>
    mutate(scen_key  = scen_key,
           year      = year(date),
           age_class = floor(age),
           peak_weight = weight / condition)
}

# Helper: compute per-year biomass accrual by patch (experimental period only).
# Summarises to n_years × 2 rows per scenario before combining.
compute_patch_growth <- function(ibm_long, scen_key) {
  if (ibm_is_empty(ibm_long)) return(tibble())
  ibm_long |>
    filter(date >= exp_start_date, !is.na(ggd)) |>
    mutate(daily_growth_g = weight * ggd, year = year(date)) |>
    group_by(year, patch) |>
    summarise(total_g = sum(daily_growth_g, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(scen_key = scen_key)
}

# ── Oct 1 census: experimental period, all hab types, all scenarios ───────────
exp_oct1 <- purrr::map_dfr(ibm_list_mech, function(scen) {
  extract_oct1_exp(scen$df, pc_to_key(scen$pc)) |>
    mutate(hab_type = scen$ht)
}) |>
  left_join(scen_meta, by = "scen_key") |>
  mutate(
    label    = factor(label,    levels = scen_meta$label),
    hab_type = factor(hab_type, levels = c("Cold only", "Cold + Warm", "Cold + Warm (high P)"))
  )

# ── Annual biomass accrual by patch, all hab types, all scenarios ─────────────
patch_growth <- purrr::map_dfr(ibm_list_mech, function(scen) {
  compute_patch_growth(scen$df, pc_to_key(scen$pc)) |>
    mutate(hab_type = scen$ht)
}) |>
  left_join(scen_meta, by = "scen_key") |>
  mutate(
    label    = factor(label,    levels = scen_meta$label),
    hab_type = factor(hab_type, levels = c("Cold only", "Cold + Warm", "Cold + Warm (high P)"))
  )

# ── Annual population totals per scenario × hab_type × year ──────────────────
exp_pop_yr <- exp_oct1 |>
  group_by(hab_type, label, prop_cold, year) |>
  summarise(n = n(), biomass_kg = sum(weight) / 1000, .groups = "drop")

# ── Annual adult (peak weight > 200g) totals per scenario × hab_type × year ──
exp_adult_yr <- exp_oct1 |>
  filter(peak_weight >= 200) |>
  group_by(hab_type, label, prop_cold, year) |>
  summarise(n = n(), biomass_kg = sum(weight) / 1000, .groups = "drop")

# ── Annual spawner totals per scenario × hab_type × year ─────────────────────
# Each parent may appear multiple times per year (repeat spawning attempts);
# average weight within (year, parent) before summing to avoid double-counting mass.
exp_spawn_yr <- purrr::map_dfr(ibm_list_mech, function(scen) {
  scen$spawn_log |>
    mutate(date = base_params$mindate + (dayofsim - 1L),
           yr   = year(date)) |>
    filter(date >= exp_start_date) |>
    group_by(yr, parent_pid) |>
    summarise(parent_wt = mean(weight), .groups = "drop") |>
    group_by(yr) |>
    summarise(n_spawners    = n_distinct(parent_pid),
              biom_spawn_kg = sum(parent_wt) / 1000,
              .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(hab_type = scen$ht, prop_cold = scen$pc)
}) |>
  left_join(scen_meta, by = "prop_cold") |>
  mutate(
    label    = factor(label,    levels = scen_meta$label),
    hab_type = factor(hab_type, levels = c("Cold only", "Cold + Warm", "Cold + Warm (high P)"))
  )
```


## Population outcomes

### Summary of key metrics

Maximum age and size are the annual 95th percentiles of age and weight in the Oct 1 census (experimental period), shown as the mean and SD among years. Age at first reproduction is the mean and SD, among individual parents whose first spawn occurred in the experimental period, of the age at their first `spawn_log` entry (founder fish with no recorded birth are excluded). Spawning participation is the number of spawners in a year divided by the Oct 1 census population size of the previous year, shown as the mean and SD among years. Error bars are $$\\pm$$ 1 SD, truncated at zero. Missing bars are scenarios that went extinct (or, for 100% cold, have no warm-habitat run).

```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 7

# Parent birth day = dayofsim of the spawning event whose offspring pid range contains it.
# Age increases with dayofsim, so each parent's first spawn has its minimum age.
first_repro <- purrr::map_dfr(ibm_list_mech, function(scen) {
  sl <- scen$spawn_log
  births <- sl |>
    distinct(dayofsim, offspring_pid_start, offspring_pid_end) |>
    rename(birth_day = dayofsim)

  sl |>
    mutate(date = base_params$mindate + (dayofsim - 1L)) |>
    left_join(births, by = join_by(between(parent_pid, offspring_pid_start, offspring_pid_end))) |>
    # Founder fish have no recorded birth
    filter(!is.na(birth_day)) |>
    arrange(parent_pid, dayofsim) |>
    distinct(parent_pid, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
    filter(date >= exp_start_date) |>
    transmute(parent_pid,
              age_first = (dayofsim - birth_day) / 365,
              hab_type  = scen$ht,
              prop_cold = scen$pc)
}) |>
  left_join(scen_meta, by = "prop_cold") |>
  mutate(label    = factor(label,    levels = scen_meta$label),
         hab_type = factor(hab_type, levels = levels(exp_oct1$hab_type)))

# Full scenario grid so bars stay aligned when a scenario is missing
summ_grid <- expand_grid(hab_type = levels(exp_oct1$hab_type), label = scen_meta$label) |>
  mutate(hab_type = factor(hab_type, levels = levels(exp_oct1$hab_type)),
         label    = factor(label,    levels = scen_meta$label))

# Mean and SD among years of the annual 95th percentiles
summ_max <- exp_oct1 |>
  group_by(hab_type, label, year) |>
  summarise(max_age = quantile(age, 0.99),
            max_wt  = quantile(weight, 0.99),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(hab_type, label) |>
  summarise(max_age_mean = mean(max_age), max_age_sd = sd(max_age),
            max_wt_mean  = mean(max_wt),  max_wt_sd  = sd(max_wt),
            .groups = "drop")

# Mean and SD among individual parents
summ_repro <- first_repro |>
  group_by(hab_type, label) |>
  summarise(age_first_mean = mean(age_first), age_first_sd = sd(age_first),
            .groups = "drop")

# Spawners in year y relative to the Oct 1 census of year y - 1;
# mean and SD among years
summ_part <- exp_spawn_yr |>
  inner_join(exp_pop_yr |> transmute(hab_type, label, yr = year + 1L, n_census = n),
             by = c("hab_type", "label", "yr")) |>
  mutate(participation = n_spawners / n_census) |>
  group_by(hab_type, label) |>
  summarise(participation_mean = mean(participation), participation_sd = sd(participation),
            .groups = "drop")

summ_all <- summ_grid |>
  left_join(summ_max,   by = c("hab_type", "label")) |>
  left_join(summ_repro, by = c("hab_type", "label")) |>
  left_join(summ_part,  by = c("hab_type", "label"))

bar_plot <- function(y_var, y_lab) {
  ggplot(summ_all, aes(x = label, y = .data[[paste0(y_var, "_mean")]], fill = hab_type)) +
    geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.75,
             color = "black", linewidth = 0.3, na.rm = TRUE) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = pmax(0, .data[[paste0(y_var, "_mean")]] - .data[[paste0(y_var, "_sd")]]),
                      ymax = .data[[paste0(y_var, "_mean")]] + .data[[paste0(y_var, "_sd")]]),
                  position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.3, linewidth = 0.4, na.rm = TRUE) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = hab_cols, name = "Scenario", drop = FALSE) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = y_lab) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
    theme(panel.grid = element_blank(),
          axis.text = element_text(color = "black"),
          axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
}

(bar_plot("max_age",       "Maximum age (99th percentile, yr)") +
   bar_plot("max_wt",        "Maximum size (99th percentile, g)") +
   bar_plot("age_first",     "Mean age at first reproduction (yr)") +
   bar_plot("participation", "Mean spawning participation")) +
  plot_layout(ncol = 2, guides = "collect") +
  plot_annotation(title = "Summary of key population metrics")
```

### Abundance and biomass

Mean Oct 1 (census) and annual spawning abundance and biomass during the experimental period, as a function of the proportion of cold habitat and habitat scenario. Spawner counts and biomass are derived from the spawn_log (i.e., we know exactly who spawns). 

```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 7

# Add zero rows for scenarios that went extinct (absent from the summaries).
# CV is undefined at zero abundance, so it is left NA.
add_extinct_zeros <- function(sum_tbl) {
  extinct_rows <- scen_extinct |>
    filter(extinct) |>
    mutate(prop_cold = as.numeric(scen_key) / 100) |>
    left_join(scen_meta |> select(prop_cold, label), by = "prop_cold") |>
    transmute(hab_type = factor(hab_type, levels = levels(sum_tbl$hab_type)),
              label    = factor(label,    levels = levels(sum_tbl$label)),
              prop_cold,
              mean_n = 0, sd_n = 0, mean_b = 0, sd_b = 0)
  sum_tbl |>
    bind_rows(anti_join(extinct_rows, sum_tbl, by = c("hab_type", "prop_cold"))) |>
    arrange(hab_type, desc(prop_cold))
}

# summarize total population
pop_sum <- exp_pop_yr |>
  group_by(hab_type, label, prop_cold) |>
  summarise(
    mean_n  = mean(n),
    sd_n    = sd(n),
    cv_n    = sd(n) / mean(n),
    mean_b  = mean(biomass_kg),
    sd_b    = sd(biomass_kg),
    cv_b    = sd(biomass_kg) / mean(biomass_kg),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  add_extinct_zeros()

write_csv(pop_sum, "pop_sum.csv")

# summarize adult population

  summarise(

    mean_b  = mean(biomass_kg),
    sd_b    = sd(biomass_kg),
    cv_b    = sd(biomass_kg) / mean(biomass_kg),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  add_extinct_zeros()

# summarize spawning population

  summarise(
    mean_n  = mean(n_spawners),

    cv_n    = sd(n_spawners)    / mean(n_spawners),
    mean_b  = mean(biom_spawn_kg),

  ) |>
  add_extinct_zeros()

# function to create x-axis

# plotting function
ab_plot <- function(data, y_var, y_err, y_lab, title_str, y_limits) {
  p <- ggplot(data, aes(x = prop_cold, y = .data[[y_var]], color = hab_type)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dotted") +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = pmax(0, .data[[y_var]] - .data[[y_err]]), ymax = .data[[y_var]] + .data[[y_err]]), width = 0.05, linewidth = 0.6, position = position_dodge(width = 0.03)) +
    geom_line(aes(linetype = hab_type, group = hab_type), linetype = "solid", linewidth = 0.8, position = position_dodge(width = 0.03)) +
    geom_point(aes(shape = hab_type, fill = hab_type), size = 3, shape = 21, color = "black", position = position_dodge(width = 0.03)) +
    scale_color_manual(values = hab_cols, name = "Scenario") +

    labs(y = y_lab, title = title_str) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
    theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text = element_text(color = "black")) + 
    scale_y_continuous(limits = y_limits)
  p
}
```

#### Marginal benefits

View the absolute and relative differences in total and spawning population abundance and biomass between cold+warm/high P and cold-only scenarios.
```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 7
#| 
plot_scenario_diff <- function(data, metric, type = c("absolute", "relative"), y_limits = NULL, title_str = NULL) {
  type <- match.arg(type)

  metric_label <- switch(metric, mean_n = "abundance (N)", mean_b = "biomass (kg)")
  y_label <- if (type == "absolute") {
    paste("Absolute diff. in", metric_label)
  } else {
    paste("Relative diff. in", metric_label)
  }

  df <- data |>
    select(hab_type, label, prop_cold, all_of(metric)) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = hab_type, values_from = all_of(metric)) |>
    rename(cold_only = "Cold only", cold_warm = "Cold + Warm", high_P = "Cold + Warm (high P)")

  if (type == "absolute") {
    df <- df |>
      mutate(ad_coldwarm = cold_warm - cold_only,
             ad_highp    = high_P   - cold_only) |>
      pivot_longer(ad_coldwarm:ad_highp, names_to = "hab_type", values_to = "diff") |>
      mutate(hab_type = recode(hab_type,
               "ad_coldwarm" = "Cold + Warm", "ad_highp" = "Cold + Warm (high P)"))
  } else {
    df <- df |>
      # Relative difference is undefined where cold-only is 0 (extinct); drop those points
      filter(cold_only > 0) |>
      mutate(rd_coldwarm = (cold_warm - cold_only) / cold_only,
             rd_highp    = (high_P   - cold_only) / cold_only) |>
      pivot_longer(rd_coldwarm:rd_highp, names_to = "hab_type", values_to = "diff") |>
      mutate(hab_type = recode(hab_type,
               "rd_coldwarm" = "Cold + Warm", "rd_highp" = "Cold + Warm (high P)"))
  }

  p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = prop_cold, y = diff, color = hab_type)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
    geom_line(aes(group = hab_type), linetype = "solid", linewidth = 0.8, position = position_dodge(width = 0.03)) +
    # geom_point(size = 3, shape = 16, position = position_dodge(width = 0.03)) +
    geom_point(aes(shape = hab_type, fill = hab_type), size = 3, shape = 21, color = "black", position = position_dodge(width = 0.03)) +
    scale_color_manual(values = hab_cols, name = "Scenario") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = hab_cols, name = "Scenario") +
    labs(y = y_label, title = title_str) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
    theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text = element_text(color = "black")) +
    cold_x("Proportion cold habitat")

  if (type == "absolute") {
    p <- p + scale_y_continuous(
      limits = y_limits
    )
  }
  
  if (type == "relative") {
    p <- p + scale_y_continuous(
      labels = scales::label_percent(accuracy = 1),
      limits = y_limits
    )
  }

  p
}

# Absolute difference: Abundance
p_ab_n       <- plot_scenario_diff(pop_sum,   "mean_n", type = "absolute", y_limits = c(0,150), title_str = "Total")
p_ab_n_ad    <- plot_scenario_diff(adult_sum, "mean_n", type = "absolute", y_limits = c(0,150), title_str = "Adults (>200g)")
p_ab_n_sp    <- plot_scenario_diff(spawn_sum, "mean_n", type = "absolute", y_limits = c(0,150), title_str = "Spawners")

p_ab_b_sp    <- plot_scenario_diff(spawn_sum, "mean_b", type = "absolute", y_limits = c(0,125))

# Relative difference: Abundance

p_re_n_ad    <- plot_scenario_diff(adult_sum, "mean_n", "relative", y_limits = c(0,8), title_str = "Adults (>200g)")
p_re_n_sp    <- plot_scenario_diff(spawn_sum, "mean_n", "relative", y_limits = c(0,8), title_str = "Spawners")

# Relative difference: Biomass

((p_ab_n + theme(axis.title.x = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_blank())) +
```

### Size structure

#### Variation in weight

Coarse descriptors of the variation or diversity in body sizes among habitat scenarios and cold habitat proportions. The Gini coefficient describes the inequality in a distribution, where 0 means that all fish same size, where 1 indicates maximum inequality (this metric is not sensitive to the mean). 

```{r}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 7

# year specific summaries
varwt_yr <- exp_oct1 %>% 
  group_by(hab_type, label, prop_cold, year) %>%
  summarise(mean_weight = mean(weight),
            sd_weight = sd(log(weight)), 
            range_weight = range(weight)[2] - range(weight)[1],
            cv_weight = sd(weight) / mean(weight)) %>%
  ungroup()

# varwt_summ <- exp_oct1 %>% 
#   group_by(hab_type, label, prop_cold) %>%
#   summarise(mean_weight = mean(weight),
#             sd_weight = sd(weight), 
#             range_weight = range(weight)[2] - range(weight)[1],
#             cv_weight = sd(weight) / mean(weight)) %>%
#   ungroup()

# summarize over years: means of year-specific summary stats. If we just calculate as year-agnostic, the ranges get messup up
varwt_summ <- varwt_yr %>% 
  group_by(hab_type, label, prop_cold) %>%
  summarise(mean_weight = mean(mean_weight),
            sd_weight = mean(sd_weight), 
            range_weight = mean(range_weight),
            cv_weight = mean(cv_weight)) %>%
  ungroup()


#### Gini coefficient describes the inequality in a distribtion: 0 = all fish same size, 1 = maximum inequality (not sensitive to mean) 

gini <- function(x) {
  x <- sort(x[!is.na(x)])
  n <- length(x)
  (2 * sum(seq_len(n) * x) / (n * sum(x))) - (n + 1) / n
}

gini_yr <- exp_oct1 |>
  group_by(hab_type, label, prop_cold, year) |>
  summarise(gini = gini(weight), .groups = "drop")

gini_summ <- gini_yr |>
  group_by(hab_type, label, prop_cold) |>
  summarise(gini = mean(gini), .groups = "drop")

p_gini <- ggplot() +
  geom_point(data = gini_yr,
             aes(x = prop_cold, y = gini, color = hab_type),
             shape = 16, alpha = 0.5,
             position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.05, dodge.width = 0.07)) +
  geom_line(data = gini_summ,
            aes(x = prop_cold, y = gini, color = hab_type, group = hab_type),
            linewidth = 0.85, position = position_dodge(width = 0.07)) +
  geom_point(data = gini_summ,
             aes(x = prop_cold, y = gini, fill = hab_type),
             shape = 21, size = 3, color = "black",
             position = position_dodge(width = 0.07)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = hab_cols, name = "Scenario") +
  scale_fill_manual( values = hab_cols, name = "Scenario") +
  cold_x("Proportion cold habitat") +
  labs(y = "Gini coefficient",
       title = "(d)") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text = element_text(color = "black"),
        legend.position = "right")


#### Plotting 

# function to create x-axis
cold_x <- function(xlab = NULL) {
  list(
    scale_x_continuous(
      breaks = scen_meta$prop_cold,
      labels = scales::label_percent(accuracy = 1),
      limits = c(0, 1),
      transform = "reverse"
    ),
    labs(x = xlab)
  )
}

# Shared scale additions for hab_type encoding (linetype + shape merged legend)
hab_scales <- list(
  scale_linetype_manual(values = hab_lty,   name = "Habitat"),
  scale_shape_manual(  values = hab_shape,  name = "Habitat")
)

# plotting function
sizevar_plot <- function(y_var, y_lab, title_str) {
  p <- ggplot() + 
  geom_point(data = varwt_yr, aes(x = prop_cold, y = .data[[y_var]], color = hab_type),
             shape = 16, alpha = 0.5, position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.05, dodge.width = 0.07)) + 
  geom_line(data = varwt_summ, aes(x = prop_cold, y = .data[[y_var]], color = hab_type, group = hab_type),
            linewidth = 0.85, position = position_dodge(width = 0.07)) +
  geom_point(data = varwt_summ, aes(x = prop_cold, y = .data[[y_var]], fill = hab_type),
             shape = 21, size = 3, color = "black", position = position_dodge(width = 0.07)) +
  scale_color_manual(values  = hab_cols, name = "Scenario") +
  scale_fill_manual(values  = hab_cols, name = "Scenario") +
  labs(y = y_lab, title = title_str) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text = element_text(color = "black"))
  p
}

# generate plots
p1 <- sizevar_plot(y_var = "mean_weight", y_lab = "Mean weight (g)",  title_str = "(a)") + cold_x()
p2 <- sizevar_plot(y_var = "sd_weight", y_lab = "Standard deviation of log(weights)",  title_str = "(b)") + cold_x()
p3 <- sizevar_plot(y_var = "range_weight", y_lab = "Range of weights (g)",  title_str = "(c)") + cold_x("Proportion cold habitat")
p4 <- sizevar_plot(y_var = "cv_weight", y_lab = "CV of weights",  title_str = "(d)") + cold_x("Proportion cold habitat")

# combine plots
(p1 + p2) / (p3 + p_gini) +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect") &
  theme(legend.position = "right")
```

Together, these panels show that warm habitat availability increases both mean body size and the diversity of body sizes (panels a–c), with somewhat complex effects on body-size inequality (panel d).


#### Size spectra

Body-size frequency distributions across habitat scenarios and cold proportions, based on all Oct 1 individual records from the experimental period. Larger fish should be more frequent in cold+warm and high-P scenarios if warm habitat provides a survival benefit that allows individuals to accumulate growth over more years.

Survival function (complementary CDF): P(weight ≥ x) on log-log axes, summarized across years. Quantiles are computed per year at a fixed exceedance probability grid, then averaged across years; the ribbon spans ±1 SD. If cold+warm or high-P scenarios support more large fish, their lines will lie above cold-only at large x. Note that the 5% cold panel has small per-year sample sizes (10–48 fish/year), so its ribbons are wider.

```{r}

# Fixed exceedance probability grid

# Per-year quantile of weight at each exceedance probability
surv_yr <- exp_oct1 |>
  group_by(hab_type, label, year) |>
  reframe(
    p_exceed = rev(p_grid),
    q        = quantile(weight, probs = 1 - rev(p_grid))

    sd_q   = sd(q),
    .groups = "drop"
```

#### Growth: weight-at-age

Shifts in size spectra could driven by changes in growth regimes: mean weight-at-age.

Mean weight at each integer age class, pooled across all Oct 1 experimental-period censuses, compared across scenarios. Lines colored from blue (cold-dominant) to red/orange (warm-dominant). Means are only calculated for age classes with 5 or more individuals.

*Note that warm habitat doesn't appear to appreciably benefit maximum/asymptotic size until 50% cold, likely because access to warm habitats benefits juvenile growth (and perhaps survival?), and this slows growth of older individuals via density dependence.*

*There also appears to be a pretty clear growth-survival trade-off among scenarios: as warm habitat becomes increasingly available relative to cold habitat, fish grow larger but survival/maximum age decreases. (below, we will see that this is driven by increasing summer mortality on older, larger individuals as these larger fish require increasingly greater consumption/p-values for maintenance)*

#### Age structure

Shifts in size spectra could also be driving by shifting age structure. 

(Top) Mean proportion of total abundance at each age class during the experimental period, compared across scenarios.(Bottom) Difference in proportional abundance at each age class relative to cold-only, averaged across years. Negative values indicate age classes that are proportionally less abundant in warm-habitat scenarios; positive values indicate age classes that are proportionally more abundant. 

```{r}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 6

# Per-year counts and biomass by age class (fill zeros for absent classes)
age_yr_scen <- exp_oct1 |>
  group_by(hab_type, label, prop_cold, year, age_class) |>
  summarise(n = n(), biomass_kg = sum(weight) / 1000, .groups = "drop") |>
  complete(nesting(hab_type, label, prop_cold), year, age_class,
           fill = list(n = 0, biomass_kg = 0))

# Per-year proportional abundance — shared by absolute and difference plots
prop_n_yr <- age_yr_scen |>
  group_by(hab_type, label, prop_cold, year) |>
  mutate(prop_n = n / sum(n)) |>
  ungroup()

# Cold-only reference proportions for difference plot
cold_ref <- prop_n_yr |>
  filter(hab_type == "Cold only") |>
  select(label, year, age_class, prop_ref = prop_n)

# Proportional abundance summarised across years
prop_n_scen <- prop_n_yr |>
  group_by(hab_type, label, prop_cold, age_class) |>
  summarise(mean_prop = mean(prop_n), sd_prop = sd(prop_n), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(mean_prop > 0)

# Proportional biomass by age class
prop_b_scen <- age_yr_scen |>
  group_by(hab_type, label, prop_cold, year) |>
  mutate(prop = biomass_kg / sum(biomass_kg)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  group_by(hab_type, label, prop_cold, age_class) |>
  summarise(mean_prop = mean(prop), sd_prop = sd(prop), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(mean_prop > 0)

# Difference from cold-only, summarised across years
# (prop_n_yr and cold_ref computed in the chunk above)
diff_n_scen <- prop_n_yr |>
  filter(hab_type != "Cold only") |>
  left_join(cold_ref, by = c("label", "year", "age_class")) |>
  mutate(diff = prop_n - prop_ref) |>
  group_by(hab_type, label, prop_cold, age_class) |>
  summarise(
    mean_diff = mean(diff, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_diff   = sd(diff,   na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups   = "drop"
  )

# Panels with no valid difference: 100% cold has no warm run to compare, and any
# scenario whose cold-only reference went extinct has all-NaN differences.
# Add a placeholder row for labels absent from diff_n_scen so facets align with the top row.
diff_no_data <- diff_n_scen |>
  group_by(label) |>
  filter(all(is.na(mean_diff))) |>
  distinct(label) |>
  bind_rows(tibble(label = setdiff(scen_meta$label, as.character(diff_n_scen$label)))) |>
  mutate(label = factor(label, levels = scen_meta$label),
         note  = "No valid\ncomparison")

diff_n_scen <- diff_n_scen |>
  bind_rows(
    tibble(label = setdiff(scen_meta$label, as.character(diff_n_scen$label)),
           hab_type = "Cold + Warm")
  ) |>
  mutate(label = factor(label, levels = scen_meta$label))
```

The dominant patterns. At moderate cold proportions (75-50%), there are proportionally fewer young fish and more old fish, indicating that this amount of warm habitat benefits adult survival. This pattern switches at low cold proportions and under high-P, where there are proportionally more young fish and fewer older fish, consistent with previous findings that adult survival may decrease under these conditions.


#### Counterfactual decomposition of size spectra

To attribute the shift in P(size) across habitat types to its two components — age structure and growth — four synthetic populations are constructed for each scenario via resampling:

| Synthetic population | Age structure from | Growth (P(size\|age)) from | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Observed cold | Cold only | Cold only | Reference |
| CF: growth effect | Cold only | Alt | What if growth shifted but age structure didn't? |
| CF: age structure effect | Alt | Cold only | What if age structure shifted but growth didn't? |
| Observed alt | Alt | Alt | Full warm-habitat effect |

Age structure determines line color (blue = cold-only ages, orange/red = warm-habitat ages); solid = observed, dashed = counterfactual. If the dashed line of a given color lies close to the solid line of the *other* color, that component alone explains most of the shift.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4
#| label: fig-cfact-cw

set.seed(3847)
n_draws <- 20000

# Empirical age-class probabilities per hab_type × label
age_probs_cf <- exp_oct1 |>
  count(hab_type, label, age_class) |>
  group_by(hab_type, label) |>
  mutate(p_age = n / sum(n)) |>
  ungroup()

# Weight pools as nested lists for fast sampling
weight_pools_cf <- exp_oct1 |>
  select(hab_type, label, age_class, weight) |>
  group_by(hab_type, label, age_class) |>
  summarise(weights = list(weight), .groups = "drop")

# Sample ages from age_hab; sample weights from wt_hab's empirical P(size | age)
draw_cf <- function(age_hab, wt_hab, focal_label, n = n_draws) {
  ap   <- age_probs_cf  |> filter(hab_type == age_hab, label == focal_label)
  wp   <- weight_pools_cf |> filter(hab_type == wt_hab,  label == focal_label)
  ages <- sample(ap$age_class, size = n, replace = TRUE, prob = ap$p_age)
  wts  <- numeric(n)
  for (a in unique(ages)) {
    idx      <- which(ages == a)
    pool_row <- which(wp$age_class == a)
    if (length(pool_row) == 0) { wts[idx] <- NA_real_; next }
    wts[idx] <- sample(wp$weights[[pool_row]], length(idx), replace = TRUE)
  }
  wts
}

compute_ccdf_vec <- function(w, n_grid = 300) {
  p_cum <- seq(0.001, 0.999, length.out = n_grid)
  tibble(q = quantile(w, probs = p_cum, na.rm = TRUE), p_exceed = 1 - p_cum)
}

# Build all counterfactual CCDFs: 5 labels × 2 alt habs × 4 scenarios
ref_hab  <- "Cold only"
alt_habs <- c("Cold + Warm", "Cold + Warm (high P)")
labs_vec <- levels(exp_oct1$label)

cf_rows <- list()
for (lab in labs_vec) {
  for (alt in alt_habs) {
    # Skip labels lacking either run (100% cold has no warm run; 5% cold-only went extinct)
    has_both <- all(c(ref_hab, alt) %in% age_probs_cf$hab_type[age_probs_cf$label == lab])
    if (!has_both) next
    scens <- list(
      list(age_h = ref_hab, wt_h = ref_hab, obs = TRUE),
      list(age_h = ref_hab, wt_h = alt,     obs = FALSE),
      list(age_h = alt,     wt_h = ref_hab, obs = FALSE),
      list(age_h = alt,     wt_h = alt,     obs = TRUE)
    )
    for (sc in scens) {
      w <- draw_cf(sc$age_h, sc$wt_h, lab)
      cf_rows[[length(cf_rows) + 1]] <- compute_ccdf_vec(w) |>
        mutate(label = lab, alt_hab = alt,
               age_hab = sc$age_h, wt_hab = sc$wt_h, observed = sc$obs)
    }
  }
}

cf_df <- bind_rows(cf_rows) |>
  mutate(label   = factor(label,   levels = levels(exp_oct1$label)),
         alt_hab = factor(alt_hab, levels = c("Cold + Warm", "Cold + Warm (high P)")))

# Plot function for one comparison pair
make_cf_plot <- function(alt, title_suffix) {
  cf_df |>
    filter(alt_hab == alt) |>
    mutate(linetype = if_else(observed, "Observed", "Counterfactual"),
           grp = interaction(age_hab, wt_hab)) |>
    ggplot(aes(x = q, y = p_exceed,
               color = age_hab, linetype = linetype, group = grp)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
    # scale_x_log10(breaks = c(10, 100, 500, 1500),
    #               labels = scales::label_number()) +
    # scale_y_log10(breaks = c(0.001, 0.01, 0.1, 1),
    #               labels = scales::label_percent(accuracy = 0.1)) +
    scale_color_manual(values = hab_cols[c("Cold only", alt)],
                       name = "Age structure from") +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = c("Observed" = "solid", "Counterfactual" = "dashed"),
                          name = NULL) +
    facet_wrap(~label, nrow = 1) +
    labs(x = "Body weight (g, log scale)", y = "P(weight \u2265 x)",
         title = paste("Counterfactual decomposition: Cold only vs.", title_suffix),
         subtitle = paste0(
           "Solid = observed  |  Dashed = counterfactual\n",
           "Blue dashed: Cold Only age structure + ", title_suffix, " growth  \u2192  growth effect alone\n",
           "Orange/red dashed: ", title_suffix,
           " age structure + Cold Only growth  \u2192  age structure effect alone"
         )) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid = element_blank(),
          axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
          plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 8.5))
}

make_cf_plot("Cold + Warm", "Cold + Warm")
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4
#| label: fig-cfact-highp

make_cf_plot("Cold + Warm (high P)", "Cold + Warm (high P)")
```

Both mechanisms contribute, but their relative importance and even their signs vary with cold-habitat proportion. Growth (mean size-at-age) is the larger driver and contributes positively across the full range of cold-habitat proportion, although contributions are small at high cold proportions. Age structure contributes as well but is the secondary mechanism and its effect is context-dependent (changes sign). At high cold proportions, age structure has a small positive effect on mean weight, consistent with increased survival and greater proportions of older individuals. But under low cold proportions, age structure has a negative effect on mean weight, consistent with previous summaries indicating reduced adult survival and a truncated age structure.

The area between two survival functions (integrated over exceedance probability) equals the difference in mean body weight — providing a scalar measure of each mechanism's contribution. Four areas are computed relative to the cold-only reference: total observed shift, growth effect (cold age structure + warm P(size|age)), age structure effect (warm age structure + cold P(size|age)), and an interaction term (residual after subtracting growth and age structure contributions). Fractional contributions are normalized by the sum of absolute component values so they always sum to 100% and are comparable across scenarios regardless of whether mechanisms act in opposing directions.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 6
#| label: fig-cfact-area


# Trapezoidal integration of area between scenario CCDF and cold-only reference
trapz_area <- function(x, y) {
  ord <- order(x); x <- x[ord]; y <- y[ord]
  sum(diff(x) * (y[-length(y)] + y[-1]) / 2)
}

q_ref <- cf_df |>
  filter(age_hab == "Cold only", wt_hab == "Cold only") |>
  select(label, alt_hab, p_exceed, q_ref = q)

area_df <- cf_df |>
  filter(!(age_hab == "Cold only" & wt_hab == "Cold only")) |>
  left_join(q_ref, by = c("label", "alt_hab", "p_exceed")) |>
  group_by(label, alt_hab, age_hab, wt_hab, observed) |>
  summarise(area = trapz_area(p_exceed, q - q_ref), .groups = "drop")

frac_df <- area_df |>
  mutate(component = case_when(
    observed == TRUE  & age_hab != "Cold only" ~ "Total",
    observed == FALSE & age_hab != "Cold only" ~ "Age structure",
    observed == FALSE & age_hab == "Cold only" ~ "Growth"
  )) |>
  select(label, alt_hab, component, area) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = component, values_from = area) |>
  mutate(`Interaction (residual)` = Total - `Age structure` - Growth) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Growth, `Age structure`, `Interaction (residual)`),
               names_to = "component", values_to = "area") |>
  mutate(
    component = factor(component, levels = c("Growth", "Age structure", "Interaction (residual)")),
    label     = factor(label, levels = levels(exp_oct1$label))
  )

ggplot(frac_df, aes(x = label, y = area, fill = component)) +
  geom_col(position = "stack") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.4) +
  # geom_segment(
  #   data = area_df |>
  #     filter(observed == TRUE, age_hab != "Cold only") |>
  #     mutate(label = factor(label, levels = levels(exp_oct1$label))),
  #   aes(x = label, xend = label, y = 0, yend = area),
  #   inherit.aes = FALSE
  # ) +
  geom_point(
    data = area_df |>
      filter(observed == TRUE, age_hab != "Cold only") |>
      mutate(label = factor(label, levels = levels(exp_oct1$label))),
    aes(x = label, y = area),
    inherit.aes = FALSE, shape = 18, size = 4
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("Growth" = "#FC8D59", "Age structure" = "#6BAED6",
               "Interaction (residual)" = "#B2DF8A"),
    name = "Mechanism"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~alt_hab, ncol = 1) +
  labs(
    x = "Cold-habitat proportion",
    y = "Contribution to mean weight shift (g)",
    title = "Decomposition of size spectrum shift (area between CCDFs)",
    subtitle = "Diamond = observed shift relative to cold-only\nBars = additive decomposition; negative bars = mechanism suppresses mean weight"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "right", panel.grid = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
```

The fractional contributions are:

```{r}
#| label: tbl-cfact-fractions

area_df |>
  mutate(component = case_when(
    observed == TRUE  & age_hab != "Cold only" ~ "Total",
    observed == FALSE & age_hab != "Cold only" ~ "Age structure",
    observed == FALSE & age_hab == "Cold only" ~ "Growth"
  )) |>
  select(label, alt_hab, component, area) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = component, values_from = area) |>
  mutate(
    Interaction       = Total - `Age structure` - Growth,
    `Total shift (g)` = round(Total, 1),
    # Denominator = sum of absolute component values so fractions always sum to 100%
    abs_total         = abs(Growth) + abs(`Age structure`) + abs(Interaction),
    `Growth (%)`        = paste0(round(abs(Growth)          / abs_total * 100, 1), "%"),
    `Age structure (%)` = paste0(round(abs(`Age structure`)  / abs_total * 100, 1), "%"),
    `Interaction (%)`   = paste0(round(abs(Interaction)      / abs_total * 100, 1), "%")
  ) |>
  select(
    `Cold proportion` = label,
    Comparison        = alt_hab,
    `Total shift (g)`,
    `Growth (%)`,
    `Age structure (%)`,
    `Interaction (%)`
  ) |>
  arrange(Comparison, `Cold proportion`) |>
  knitr::kable(
    align   = c("l", "l", "r", "r", "r", "r"),
    caption = paste(
      "Fractional contribution of each mechanism to the size spectrum shift,",
      "measured as the area between counterfactual and reference CCDFs (equivalent",
      "to the difference in mean body weight, g). Fractions are the absolute",
      "contribution of each component divided by the sum of all absolute",
      "contributions, so they always sum to 100% and reflect true relative",
      "magnitudes regardless of whether mechanisms act in opposing directions.",
      "The sign of the total shift (g) indicates the direction of the net change."
    )
  )
```

The interaction term (the residual after subtracting the growth and age-structure contributions) is not uniformly signed. Its sign and size depend on whether the two mechanisms reinforce or offset each other. At moderate cold proportions (50–25% cold) it is small and positive (+4 to +17 g, 3–9% of the summed component magnitudes). The clearest departure is at low cold proportions, especially under high P. There the interaction becomes large and negative (25% cold: −71 g, 12%; 10% cold: −164 g, 20%). This happens where the age-structure effect has turned negative (−29 and −88 g) and growth is at its largest (489 and 551 g). The negative interaction means the combined effect is sub-additive. The growth benefit of warm habitat is realized mainly by fish that survive to old ages and large sizes. Under low cold proportions, warm habitat also truncates the age structure, so the growth gain acts on a population with fewer old fish. As a result, the full effect (+388 and +300 g) is smaller than the sum of the growth and age-structure effects computed separately. In effect, the two mechanisms partly cancel each other, because the survival cost removes some of the individuals who would have carried the largest growth gains. Growth still dominates, so the net shift remains strongly positive. The same pattern appears, more weakly, in the base scenario at 10% cold (−24 g). At 95% cold the total shift is near zero (0.5 g in the base scenario, 6 g under high P). The interaction percentages there are therefore unstable and shouldn't be interpreted.


## Mechanisms and details

### Abundance

Mean monthly abundance of each birth cohort tracked from hatching through the first four years of life, averaging across all experimental-period cohort-years. The monthly resolution reveals two distinct seasonal survival bottlenecks: 

1. a steep summer decline that is common to all simulation runs
2. a winter/spring divergence between scenarios driven declines in abundance for the cold-only scenarios.

```{r cohort-abund-data}
#| cache: true

# ── Helper: monthly cohort abundance from birth through max_months ────────────
f_cohort_ts <- function(df, exp_start, max_months = 96L, birth_mo = 4L) {
  if (ibm_is_empty(df)) {
    return(tibble(msb = integer(), mean_n = double(), se_n = double(), n_coh = integer()))
  }
  exp_yr  <- year(exp_start)
  max_coh <- exp_yr + 45L
  df |>
    filter(survived == 1L, date >= exp_start, day(date) == 1L) |>
    mutate(
      yr  = year(date),
      mo  = month(date),
      msb = (yr - cohort) * 12L + (mo - birth_mo)  # months since April birth
    ) |>
    filter(msb >= 1L, msb <= max_months,
           cohort >= exp_yr, cohort <= max_coh) |>
    count(cohort, msb, name = "n") |>
    group_by(msb) |>
    summarise(mean_n = mean(n),
              se_n   = sd(n) / sqrt(n()),
              n_coh  = n(),
              .groups = "drop")
}


cohort_ts_df <- bind_rows(lapply(ibm_list_mech, \(s) {
  f_cohort_ts(s$df, exp_start_date) |>
    mutate(prop_cold = s$pc,
           hab_type  = s$ht,
           label     = scen_meta$label[scen_meta$prop_cold == s$pc])
})) |>
  mutate(
    label    = factor(label, levels = scen_meta$label),
    hab_type = factor(hab_type,
                      levels = c("Cold only", "Cold + Warm", "Cold + Warm (high P)"))
  )
```

```{r cohort-abund-plot}
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 5

# ── Seasonal shading via annotate() — bypasses fill scale entirely ────────────
# Seasons per year: May(1) | Jun-Aug(2-4)=summer | Sep-Nov(5-7)=fall
#                   Dec-Feb(8-10)=winter | Mar-Apr(11-12)=spring
# annotate() draws at fixed coordinates without routing through any fill scale,
# so geom_ribbon can use scale_fill_manual() without conflict.
make_season_layers <- function(n_years = 8L, ymin = 0.1, ymax = 1e7) {
  xmin_tmpl <- c( 0.5,  1.5,  4.5,  7.5, 10.5)
  xmax_tmpl <- c( 1.5,  4.5,  7.5, 10.5, 12.5)
  fill_tmpl <- c("#A8D5A2", "#F5C543", "#C8A96E", "#AEC6E8", "#A8D5A2")
  unlist(lapply(0:(n_years - 1L), \(y)
    lapply(seq_along(fill_tmpl), \(i)
      annotate("rect",
               xmin  = xmin_tmpl[i] + y * 12,
               xmax  = xmax_tmpl[i] + y * 12,
               ymin  = ymin, ymax = ymax,  # finite bounds required (log scale fails with -Inf/Inf)
               fill  = fill_tmpl[i],
               alpha = 0.22)
    )
  ), recursive = FALSE)
}

yr_lines  <- tibble(msb = c(12L, 24L, 36L, 48L, 60L, 72L, 84L, 96L)+1)
hab_cols  <- c("Cold only"            = "#6BAED6",
               "Cold + Warm"          = "#FC8D59",
               "Cold + Warm (high P)" = "#B30000")


ggplot(cohort_ts_df,
       aes(x = msb, y = mean_n, color = hab_type, group = hab_type)) +
  make_season_layers(8L) +
  # geom_vline(data = yr_lines, aes(xintercept = msb),
  #            inherit.aes = FALSE,
  #            linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.4, color = "grey40") +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = pmax(0.5, mean_n - 1.96 * se_n),
                  ymax = mean_n + 1.96 * se_n,
                  fill = hab_type),
              alpha = 0.20, color = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.85) +
  # geom_point(data = \(d) filter(d, msb %in% c(1L, 6L, 13L, 18L, 25L, 30L, 37L, 42L)),
  #            size = 2.0) +
  facet_wrap(~ label, nrow = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = hab_cols, name = NULL) +
  scale_fill_manual(values  = hab_cols, name = NULL,
                    breaks  = names(hab_cols)) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(1L, 13L, 25L, 37L, 49L, 61L, 73L, 85L, 97L),
    labels = c("M\nY1", "M\nY2", "M\nY3", "M\nY4", "M\nY5", "M\nY6", "M\nY7", "M\nY8", "M\nY9"),
    minor_breaks = NULL) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  # coord_cartesian clips the view to the data range without affecting the
  # annotate rectangles (which extend to ymax = 1e7 to fill the panel)
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(
    min(cohort_ts_df$mean_n - 1.96 * cohort_ts_df$se_n, na.rm = TRUE) * 0.9,
    max(cohort_ts_df$mean_n + 1.96 * cohort_ts_df$se_n, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.1
  )) +
  labs(
    x       = NULL,
    y       = "Mean cohort abundance (log scale, \u00b195% CI)",

                    "| Winter (blue) | Spring (green).",

```

Monthly log-scale slope (the first-difference of log cohort abundance between consecutive monthly snapshots) shows when proportional losses are highest. The y-axis is clipped to reveal post-bottleneck structure; summer Year-1 spikes (birth-pulse to October; range $\approx -0.5$ to $-2.5$) exceed the visible range and are noted with an arrow.

```{r cohort-slope-plot}
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 5

slope_monthly_df <- cohort_ts_df |>
  arrange(label, hab_type, msb) |>
  group_by(label, hab_type) |>
  mutate(
    msb_mid  = (msb + lead(msb)) / 2,
    slope    = log(lead(mean_n)) - log(mean_n),
    se_slope = sqrt((lead(se_n) / lead(mean_n))^2 + (se_n / mean_n)^2),
    lo95     = slope - 1.96 * se_slope,
    hi95     = slope + 1.96 * se_slope
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(slope)) |>
  ungroup()

y_clip_lo <- -0.35
y_clip_hi <-  0.08

ggplot(slope_monthly_df,
       aes(x = msb_mid, y = slope, color = hab_type, group = hab_type)) +
  # Seasonal bands: use finite y bounds spanning the clipped axis range
  make_season_layers(8L, ymin = y_clip_lo - 0.05, ymax = y_clip_hi + 0.05) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.4, color = "grey30") +
  geom_vline(data = yr_lines, aes(xintercept = msb),
             inherit.aes = FALSE,
             linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.4, color = "grey40") +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = pmax(lo95, y_clip_lo),
                  ymax = pmin(hi95, y_clip_hi),
                  fill = hab_type),
              alpha = 0.18, color = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  # Arrow marking clipped summer spikes
  annotate("segment",
           x = 1.5, xend = 1.5, y = y_clip_lo + 0.04, yend = y_clip_lo + 0.005,
           arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.15, "cm"), type = "closed"),
           color = "grey30") +
  annotate("text", x = 2.2, y = y_clip_lo + 0.05,
           label = "Summer Y1 spikes clipped\n(range \u22120.5 to \u22122.5)",
           size = 2.5, color = "grey30", hjust = 0) +
  facet_wrap(~ label, nrow = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = hab_cols, name = NULL) +
  scale_fill_manual(values  = hab_cols, name = NULL,
                    breaks  = names(hab_cols)) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(1L, 13L, 25L, 37L, 49L, 61L, 73L, 85L, 97L),
    labels = c("M\nY1", "M\nY2", "M\nY3", "M\nY4", "M\nY5", "M\nY6", "M\nY7", "M\nY8", "M\nY9"),
    minor_breaks = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_number(accuracy = 0.1)) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(y_clip_lo, y_clip_hi)) +
  labs(
    x       = NULL,
    y       = "Monthly log-scale slope\n[log N(t+1) \u2212 log N(t)]",
    title   = "Monthly proportional decline rate",
    caption = paste(
      "Birth/spring (tan) | Summer (yellow) | Fall (brown) | Winter (blue) | Spring (green).",
      "More negative = faster proportional loss. Ribbons = \u00b195% CI.",
      "n \u2248 45 cohort-years per scenario."
    )
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    strip.background   = element_rect(fill = "grey92"),
    axis.text.x        = element_text(size = 8.5),
    legend.position    = "bottom"
  )
```

The bar chart below shows raw monthly slopes for the first 18 months of life (birth through October of year 2), preserving the within- and between-year structure to identify which months drive the greatest proportional losses. The plots clearly reveal two demographic bottlenecks: (1) major declines during May-August under all habitat scenarios and cold proportions (this is more severe and extends into September for cold+warm scenarios), and (2) smaller, but significant declines during the following March/April, but only for cold-only scenarios.

### Reproduction and recruitment

Distribution of spawning dates (day of year of fry birth) pooled across all experimental-period cohort-years, shown by scenario class and cold proportion. ()
```{r eval=FALSE}
#| cache: false

# Birth events only — filtered and immediately aggregated to doy counts to
# avoid carrying 18 M individual rows forward into geom_density()
f_spawn_dates <- function(df) {
  if (ibm_is_empty(df)) return(tibble(doy = integer(), n = integer()))
  df |>
    filter(!is.na(parent_pid),
           dayofsim == birth_dayofsim,
           date >= exp_start_date) |>
    mutate(doy = yday(date)) |>
    count(doy, name = "n")
}

# Pre-aggregate: one row per (scenario, cold proportion, doy)
spawn_date_df <- bind_rows(lapply(ibm_list_mech, \(s) {
  f_spawn_dates(s$df) |>
    mutate(prop_cold = s$pc,
           hab_type  = s$ht,
           label     = scen_meta$label[scen_meta$prop_cold == s$pc])
})) |>
  mutate(
    label    = factor(label, levels = scen_meta$label),
    hab_type = factor(hab_type,
                      levels = c("Cold + Warm (high P)", "Cold + Warm", "Cold only"))
  ) |>
  group_by(hab_type, label) |>
  mutate(density = n / sum(n)) |>   # normalise to density within each group
  ungroup()
```
